name: Cinnamon-Ginger Spiced Pork Chop with Sesame Snap Peas & Rice

instructions.primary_message: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate; season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 pork chops, boneless
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add chops and cook until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side.
Meanwhile, wash and dry ginger. Peel and mince ginger and garlic; transfer both to a small bowl.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 (1 inch) pieces ginger root
3 cloves garlic

instructions.primary_message: Add broth, soy sauce, additional oil, honey, and cinnamon to the bowl with the garlic and ginger; whisk to combine the sauce.
instructions.secondary_message:
12 fl oz (1 ½ cups) chicken or vegetable broth
⅓ cup tamari soy sauce
toasted sesame oil
1 tbsp honey

instructions.primary_message: When the chops are done, remove to a clean plate and cover with aluminum foil.
Pour sauce into the skillet and cook, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer and cook until slightly thickened, about 4 minutes.
While the sauce thickens, wash, dry, and trim snap peas.
Add snap peas to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender-crisp, 3-4 minutes.
To serve, divide rice, pork chops, snap peas, and sauce between plates. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and enjoy!
